strengths: Well-motivated practical problem with clear commercial relevance; video object insertion is challenging and important for content creation.
Sensible two-stage pipeline separating geometric reasoning (mask generation) from photorealistic synthesis, with intuitive user control through interactive placement.
4D-aware mask generation using Uni4D effectively handles geometric consistency, camera motion, and occlusions better than simple spatial masking approaches.
ROSE++ dataset construction is clever: repurposing an object-removal dataset with VLM-based object retrieval to create insertion training triplets avoids copy-paste artifacts.

Comprehensive experimental evaluation including quantitative metrics (CLIP-I, DINO-I, VBench), ablation studies demonstrating each component's contribution, and a user study with consistent preference percentages.
Strong empirical results: quantitatively outperforms commercial baselines on subject consistency (CLIP-I: 0.8122 vs 0.6349 for Kling) and demonstrates improved illumination/shadow handling.
Good qualitative results showing the method handles complex occlusions better than Pika-Pro and Kling, as evidenced by the comparison figures.
First-frame guided generation strategy is effective at anchoring object fidelity and propagating consistent appearance throughout the video.
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: each core component relies heavily on existing methods (Uni4D for 4D reconstruction, standard LoRA finetuning, basic scene flow aggregation). The contribution is primarily engineering-focused rather than introducing novel computer vision insights.

Critically weak experimental comparison: only commercial tools (Pika-Pro, Kling) are compared. The paper cites relevant academic methods (GenProp [14], ObjectDrop [27], etc.) but provides no quantitative or qualitative comparison with them. This is a major limitation for a venue like ECCV.

Entirely synthetic training data (ROSE++ is 100% synthetic) raises serious questions about real-world generalization that are not adequately addressed. No experiments on cross-domain transfer or real-to-synthetic gap analysis.
Small evaluation set (50 videos, 100 with paired objects) and limited user study scope (only 10% of test videos, 20 participants). Generalization claims lack sufficient evidence.

Technical soundness concerns: (1) Scene flow aggregation (averaging K nearest points) is simplistic—no justification for K or sensitivity analysis; (2) No error analysis or theoretical justification for robustness claims; (3) How are dynamic occlusions handled when they affect the object mask itself?

Missing critical analysis: no failure cases discussed, no computational cost/inference time reported, no discussion of when the method might fail (extreme occlusions, unusual geometries, rapid lighting changes).
Multi-view consistency metric (0.5857) remains relatively low compared to other metrics, suggesting potential issues with viewpoint consistency that warrant deeper investigation.
Reproducibility concerns: code availability not mentioned, ROSE++ dataset release not confirmed, some implementation details vague (e.g., SAM2 configuration, exact network architectures).
Incomplete ablation studies: no analysis of ROSE++ dataset size effects, no ablation on reference image quality, no study of mask propagation robustness to flow estimation errors.

Overclaiming in places: statements like 'significantly outperforms' are used liberally but the improvements, while consistent, are sometimes modest on certain metrics (e.g., Motion Smoothness: 0.9916 vs 0.9940 for Kling).

strengths: Well-designed two-stage framework that sensibly separates geometric consistency (4D-aware masks) from appearance synthesis, effectively addressing the core challenges of VOI

Creative ROSE++ dataset construction that transforms object-removal into insertion by leveraging VLM-based object generation, avoiding copy-and-paste artifacts and maintaining consistency between training and inference

Comprehensive experimental validation including introduction of VOIBench benchmark, extensive quantitative metrics (CLIP-I, DINO-I, VBench), user study with 20 participants (79-87% preference), and detailed ablation studies demonstrating contribution of each component

Strong empirical results significantly outperforming commercial tools across multiple metrics (CLIP-I: 0.8122 vs 0.6349 for Kling), with practical implications for production-quality VOI in advertising and VFX

strengths: Comprehensive system design addressing genuine practical challenges in video object insertion, combining 4D-aware placement with photometric realism
Well-executed engineering with multiple complementary components (scene reconstruction, mask propagation, scene flow tracking) that work together coherently
Solid experimental evaluation including quantitative metrics, ablation studies, and user studies across six criteria with comparisons against both commercial and research baselines

Thorough ablation studies demonstrating progressive component contributions to final performance
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: Core components combine existing techniques (standard 4D reconstruction using DINO/optical flow/SAM, standard mask reprojection with SAM refinement, fine-tuned VACE-14B). The main claimed contribution (Optics-Aware Representation Alignment) is essentially mask-conditioning—a straightforward application without algorithmic depth

Overclaimed optics-aware contributions: Ablation study (Table 3) shows alignment loss provides only 1-3% PSNR improvements; optics-focused user study (Table B2) shows only 43.7% preference on shadow/reflection-rich clips, not compelling evidence of a major contribution

Incremental experimental gains: Table 1 shows CLIP-I improvement of 0.8132 vs. VACE's 0.8068 (marginal); general user study (Table B1) shows 56.54% preference across only 20 participants on 10% of test set—consistent but not compelling improvements

Significant methodological limitations: Requires manual 3D placement annotation in reference frame (major practical constraint); imperfect mask propagation artifacts acknowledged but not systematically analyzed; weak evaluation metrics (CLIP-I, DINO-I are coarse measures of photorealism)

Dataset and benchmark concerns: VOIBench (200 clips) is small by modern standards; ROSE++ construction methodology not clearly justified; no analysis of dataset biases, failure modes, or difficulty characterization

Reproducibility and practical issues: Missing implementation details (3D point sampling, prompt selection, K-NN criteria); prohibitive inference cost (4 min + 4.5 min for 832x480 resolution) discussed as limitation but not addressed; comparison fairness unclear with different baselines using different input modalities

Incomplete failure analysis: Conclusion acknowledges complex physics cases out of scope but doesn't demonstrate systematic failures; no characterization of when 4D propagation fails or when optics synthesis produces artifacts

Weak statistical rigor: No confidence intervals or significance testing for quantitative metrics; small user study (n=20) with no inter-rater reliability reported; ablation results presented without statistical validation

Unjustified design choices: K-NN scene flow aggregation lacks justification over sophisticated tracking; necessity of extended mask generation unclear when diffusion model could learn boundaries; alignment loss appears ad-hoc without theoretical motivation

Presentation issues: Paper overclaims contributions ('production-grade', 'significantly outperforming') unsupported by evidence; dense technical sections; inconsistent notation usage; user study prompts and baseline adaptations not fully detailed

strengths: Comprehensive and well-motivated system addressing genuine limitations in existing VOI approaches (lack of 4D geometric understanding and inadequate optical effect modeling)

Extensive experimental validation with new benchmark (VOIBench) and dataset (ROSE++) specifically designed for this task, plus multiple user studies demonstrating clear preference over strong baselines

Sound technical approach combining 4D scene reconstruction with optics-aware synthesis; clever use of extended masks and alignment losses to enable optical effect synthesis without explicit supervision
Clear practical value with reasonable inference time and direct applications in film production and content creation; strong quantitative results (best CLIP-1: 0.8132, DINO-1: 0.5660)
Excellent presentation with clear motivation, well-organized method description, informative visualizations, and comprehensive supplementary material with implementation details
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: individual technical components (4D reconstruction, scene flow propagation, diffusion-based synthesis) largely build on existing methods; main contribution is system integration rather than fundamental innovation
